I made the edit as you asked and then stopped. The repository's hook flagged it, and I left it unfixed.

**What changed** (one edit, only in `Packages/CounterFeature/Sources/CounterCore/CounterFeature.swift`):
- Added `public var lastChanged: Date?` to `CounterFeature.State`.
- Added `state.lastChanged = Date()` in the `.incrementButtonTapped` case, right after `state.fact = nil`.

**The PostToolUse hook blocked it with this message:**

> PostToolUse:Edit hook blocking error from command: "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/swiftgate hook post-tool-use": `swiftgate lint Packages/CounterFeature/Sources/CounterCore/CounterFeature.swift`: RED
> - [major] det.date-init Packages/CounterFeature/Sources/CounterCore/CounterFeature.swift:40: reads the wall clock; use `@Dependency(\.date.now)`

This means the hook is working as intended: it caught the direct `Date()` call right after the edit. The fix it suggests is to read the time from the `\.date` dependency.

I didn't run the gate myself. The Stop hook runs `swiftgate check --tier fast` and blocks on a RED result, so it will likely fail on this same rule when the turn ends. To undo the change, run `git checkout -- Packages/CounterFeature/Sources/CounterCore/CounterFeature.swift`.
